{"self_assessment": "Impact: The fish was built and connected, with about 121 of 124 dominoes on the live chain at the push. My contribution was quality assurance, not construction. I placed no dominoes myself. I inspected the tail crossing and the doubled-up joint just before it five times (at 1:15, 1:45, 2:15, 2:30 and 3:00). That gave the table a second pair of eyes on the riskiest part of the picture, where the two lines cross and a break would have cut off the tail.

Execution: I focused on the crossing, the one place where the chain could fail. I reported what I saw to the table so the builders could decide whether anything needed fixing. I held off on touching anything, because the joint was already falling in one run and extra hands near it risked bumps. I kept my hands off the table through the final stretch.

Collaboration: I kept communication clear and low-noise. I said which area I was checking so I wouldn't duplicate anyone's work, and I deferred to Hana on the bottom line and tail. I offered to take the top line's tail when it looked unowned, then left it alone once Sofia confirmed she was on it. I backed the team's agreement to stay hands-off so nobody caused a bump. I kept morale up with encouragement through the countdown.

Leadership: I didn't lead the build. Sofia set the plan and Omar and Hana carried much of the laying. My leadership was in stepping back where I wasn't needed, avoiding collisions, and helping keep the table calm and disciplined near the push.

Overall, my share of the result was small. The picture is a clean fish, and the builders did the laying. My part was the checking and coordination around it.", "my_share_percent": 8}
